title: Build a PDF to EPUB Converter in Python
description: A CLI tool that converts PDFs into reflowable EPUBs, with chapter detection, inline images, and an OCR fallback for scanned pages.

children.value: I wanted a PDF reflowed into a proper EPUB — the kind of book file you can actually read on an e-reader without pinch-zooming a fixed page. Most converters either butcher the layout or just don't handle scanned pages. So I built a small Python CLI,
, using PyMuPDF for extraction, Tesseract for OCR fallback, and
Pulls chapters straight from the PDF's own table of contents/outline
Falls back to a font-size heuristic (big short lines = headings) if there's no outline
Extracts text and images in reading order, reflowed into normal paragraphs
Auto-detects scanned pages (little/no text layer) and OCRs them with Tesseract
Batch mode — point it at a folder, get a folder of EPUBs back

PDFs often carry their own outline/bookmarks (what Acrobat shows as the sidebar TOC). PyMuPDF exposes this as
. If it's there, that's the most reliable source of chapter boundaries — better than guessing from font sizes.
If there's no outline, fall back to spotting headings by font size — a short line that's noticeably bigger than the surrounding body text is probably a chapter title:
And if neither works, the whole document just becomes one chapter. Three-tier fallback, always produces
gives back blocks with bounding boxes — both text and embedded images. Sort by vertical position and you get roughly the right reading order:
(same oversized-short-line heuristic as chapter detection, just per-page). Image blocks get pulled out, re-encoded as PNG, and dropped inline as
tags — so a diagram stays right next to the paragraph that references it instead of getting stripped out.
